text:
Leah: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on credits/quotas — collecting answers and a couple of open policy decisions. I'll keep this thread tight.

Diego: Awesome, thanks. First Q: do unused promo credits roll over month-to-month or expire at period end?

Leah: Promo credits will expire at the promo expiry date (typically 180 days). We're not doing monthly rollover for promotional or trial credits.

Hana: Is there any exception for academic or grants programs?

Leah: Yes — grants/academic can get a custom expiry in the billing portal. Ops will annotate contracts so the console enforces the right TTL.

Carmen: What about soft credit top-ups? For example, can we automatically grant a small grace credit when a customer runs out to avoid broken UX?

Leah: We are launching a configurable grace-topup feature: default is OFF for self-serve, ON for some enterprise tiers. Behavior: when credits < threshold, system can apply a single grace top-up (configurable amount) and send alerts. No automatic indefinite top-ups.

Diego: Will grace top-ups be billable/chargeable?

Leah: They're billable and billed at the customer's standard rates. We also log an entry in the billing history.

Hana: How do rate limits interplay with quotas if someone does a big spike (e.g., 10k embeddings requests in a minute)?

Leah: Two-layer model: 1) Rate limits = requests/sec or requests/min to protect infra. 2) Quotas = units/credits per time window. For spikes, rate limiter enforces instantaneous caps; quota consumption still happens for accepted requests. If quota would be exceeded, requests are rejected with 402 and a short message.

Carmen: Error codes — 429 vs 402 vs 403 — what's the mapping?

Leah: 429 = rate limited (try again later), 402 = quota/credits exhausted, 403 = auth/permission error. We'll add these to the API errors doc with example bodies.

Diego: Can we subscribe to webhook notifications for low credit / quota events?

Leah: Yes 10 — webhooks and console alerts will be available. Webhook payload will include account_id, api_key, quota_type, remaining_units, and suggested actions. We'll publish schema in the developer docs.

Hana: Are per-route quotas supported (e.g., embeddings vs chat)?

Leah: Yes — console supports quota scoping by route, api-key, or tag. You can also set prioritized routes (reserve X% of monthly units for a route).

Carmen: Admin UX: can a team member accidentally remove all quotas? We need safeguards.

Leah: We will add a confirmation modal for destructive quota changes and an "undo" soft-state for 24 hours. For orgs with SSO, quota changes will require 2FA for production keys by default.

Diego: Overages: if a customer exceeds quota, do we auto-bill or block?

Leah: Default self-serve = soft mode: allow a small unpaid overage up to a cap (e.g., $100) and auto-bill at next invoice. Hard mode = block when quota reached. Enterprise contracts can choose other options.

Hana: Any specifics on the free tier for embeddings? Last all-hands said increase.

Leah: Free tier updated: 25k embedding-units per month (changed from 10k). We'll add in the public FAQ.

Carmen: Will we surface remaining quota in the SDKs?

Leah: Yes 10 headers + SDK helpers. We'll return headers like `X-RW-Quota-Remaining` and `X-RW-Quota-Reset` and expose helpers in the JS/Python SDKs to parse them.

Diego: Open policy question for leadership: should promotional credits be refundable/transferable between projects under the same org?

Leah: Leadership: please weigh in. My recommendation = non-transferable by default; transfers allowed via billing support for multi-team grants.

BillingBot: Draft pricing & policy doc: https://redwood.example.com/internal/pricing-policy-v3 (internal).

Leah: Action items: Diego will draft webhook schema (due Wed), Hana will add SDK headers (PR by Thu), Carmen will draft UX guardrails (mockups by Mon). Reply here if you want to own anything.

Diego: I'll take webhook schema.

Hana: I'll do SDK changes.

Carmen: UX guardrails, yes.

Leah: Thanks all. If anyone from the all-hands still has follow-ups, drop them here and we'll loop in Finance for any pricing exceptions. :sparkles:
